title: Percentages
subtitle: Three ways of writing the same amount.
objectives: Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
Explain what per cent actually means
Find a percentage of a quantity
Read a percentage in a real context

cards.title: A percentage is not a new kind of number
cards.text: It is a fraction wearing different clothes. Out of a hundred, every time. Get that and the rest is arithmetic.

cards.title: Per cent means per hundred
cards.text: Cent is a hundred — century, centimetre, centavo. Per cent is 'for each hundred'.
points: **45%** means 45 out of every 100.
**As a fraction** that is 45/100.
**As a decimal** that is 0.45.
**Same amount.** Three spellings.

cards.title: Every capacitor has a percentage printed on it
cards.text: Pull one out of a fan and the body says something like 2.5 µF ±5%. That ± figure is its tolerance.
points: **±5% on 2.5 µF** means anywhere from 2.375 to 2.625.
**Components are never exact.** The tolerance is the promise.
**Tighter tolerance costs more**, so cheap parts say ±20%.
**A capacitor well outside its tolerance** is a failed one.

cards.title: Press a fraction. Watch the other two land
cards.text: One quantity, three names, plus what it is worth out of 60 marks.

cards.title: Per cent means per hundred
cards.alt: A chocolate bar scored into one hundred equal squares with twenty-five broken off and set beside it
cards.text: Exactly one hundred squares. Twenty-five broken off is 25% of the bar, and nothing else.

question.explain: Cent is a hundred. A percentage is always a count out of a hundred.

cards.title: Two moves, both reversible
cards.text: Decimal to percentage, multiply by 100. Percentage to decimal, divide by 100.
points: **0.6 becomes 60%** — the point moves two places right.
**85% becomes 0.85** — two places left.
**A fraction?** Divide top by bottom first.

question.text: Write 0.3 as a percentage. Digits and the % sign.
question.explain: Multiply by 100: the point moves two places right. 0.3 becomes 30%.

cards.title: Every bar in every game is a percentage
cards.text: Health, shields, download progress, battery. All of them are a part out of a whole, drawn as a bar.
points: **Half a health bar** is 50%, 0.5, or 1/2.
**A bar at 0.2 full** is 20% — one fifth.
**Percent damage** scales with the max, which is why it hurts bosses.
**The bar is the fraction**, drawn.

cards.title: Finding a percentage of something
cards.text: Turn the percentage into a decimal, then multiply. That is the whole method.
points: **10% is easy** — move the point one place left.
**5% is half of 10%.** Build the awkward ones from the easy ones.
**15% = 10% + 5%.** No calculator needed.

cards.title: Percentages decide a training week
cards.text: Coaches do not say lift heavy. They say a percentage of the most you can lift.
points: **70% of your max** is the usual working range.
**If your max is 50 kg**, that is 35 kg.
**Going to 95% every session** is how people get injured.
**The percentage scales** as you get stronger. The method does not change.

terms.def: A part of a whole written out of 100.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Per cent means per hundred. Always.
Decimal to percentage: ×100. Back again: ÷100.
A percentage of something: make it a decimal, then multiply.
10% is one place left. Build the rest from that.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 1 Math, percentages. The lesson is built on one sentence — per cent means per hundred — and everything else is presented as a consequence of it rather than as separate rules to memorise. The lab card is the centre: he presses a fraction and sees the decimal, the percentage and a real mark out of 60 land together, which is the conversion taught as one object rather than three procedures. Mental method is taught as build-from-10%, because that is what actually gets used away from a calculator.
discussion: How would you get 15% without a calculator?
Where have you seen a percentage over 100?
extension: Work out 15% of a few bills by splitting it into 10% plus 5%.
Find three percentages in a game's interface.
misconceptions: That a percentage is a different kind of number rather than a fraction.
Moving the decimal the wrong way.
